items.title: Marist: Brown +4, Acton +7 in Ohio (Oct 20 poll)
items.summary: Marist University's October Ohio survey (released Oct 20, 2026; 1,176 registered voters, fielded Oct 15-18) finds Democrat Sherrod Brown leading incumbent Sen. Jon Husted 48%-44% among likely voters in the Senate race, and Democrat Amy Acton leading Vivek Ramaswamy 50%-43% among likely voters in the governor's race. Among registered voters, Brown leads 51%-42% and Acton 51%-43%. A Bowling Green State/YouGov poll released Friday showed Acton +6 (within MoE) and CNN/SSRS had Brown +6 — second pollsters confirming the pattern. Notable wrinkle: despite her lead, 51% of respondents expect Ramaswamy to WIN the governor's race vs 45% for Acton.
items.source_name: Marist University Poll (pollster release); Newsmax; National Zero

items.title: RNC pushing $50M+ to House and Senate races off SCOTUS ruling
items.summary: The New York Times reported Oct 20 that the RNC is transferring more than $50 million to the party's House and Senate campaign committees — the largest such late transfer in at least four cycles ($8M-$31M historically). More than $44M moved mid-August to mid-October, split evenly between the NRCC and NRSC, with ~$6M more expected by Election Day. It leverages the June Supreme Court ruling striking down coordinated-spending limits. RNC Chair Joe Gruters told Newsmax the party has 'more money in the bank to spend on elections than ever before' (entered September with $126M, raised $18.5M more). AdImpact: GOP committees have aired/reserved ~$152M in coordinated ads vs ~$102M for Dems; biggest share backs Sen. Jon Husted (R-OH), while Dems' biggest share backs Sherrod Brown. RNC also spent ~$56M on canvassing/turnout, $27M on 'election integrity' efforts through early October.
items.source_name: New York Times (original); Newsmax; Election Law Blog

items.title: Axios: GOP now fears redistricting nets just one seat nationally
items.summary: Axios reported Oct 20 that House Republicans are 'quietly scaling back hopes for the 10-seat boost they sought from redistricting nationwide' — top GOP strategists now privately worry 'the great redistricting war of 2026 will net them only one seat nationwide.' Early this summer Republicans believed they'd created 16 more GOP-friendly seats (5 TX, 4 FL, 2 OH, 1 each in AL/LA/MO/NC/TN); since then, courts tossed the Missouri map, the political environment darkened (Dems +8 in WaPo/ABC polling), and GOP support collapsed among Latino voters in TX/FL — seats mapmakers counted on. Rep. Tom Emmer (R-MN): 'Texas, I'd be surprised if we got all five. Florida, I'd be shocked if we got all four.' Cook Political Report now estimates Republicans net ~4 seats from redistricting (worst case: GOP gains 7, Dems gain 6); Dems are 'supremely confident' of winning all five CA seats. Single-sourced: Axios is the only original outlet; no second outlet in a different lean category has picked up the Oct 20 piece yet.
